description: The ACP adapter's rules: what ACPAdapter does with each call, each raw stdout line of the agent, each exit and each timer, as the effects the platform carries out in order. publish assigns the published state (state, sessionID, modelName, totalTokens) and is pushed before any other effect whenever it changed, and at the end of a call; spawn launches the agent, tagged with the launch generation, and the platform answers it with spawned or spawnFailed before anything else; writeStdin writes one JSON-RPC line (compared as JSON); closeStdin and terminateAfterGrace stop it; armStartWatchdog arms the one-shot start timer; emit hands a harness event to the session. JSON-RPC ids count from 1 per adapter and are never reset by a start. A line step feeds one raw stdout line (without its newline) to the current generation; retired steps come from the generation before it. Cases named "mock agent: ..." use acp-mock-agent.py's own lines, byte for byte, and the agent command the integration tests use.
function: ACPAdapter's JSON-RPC rules ↔ powerup_core::harness::acp::adapter::AcpAdapter — input {steps: [acp step]}; expected {effects: [[acp effect]] (one list per step), snapshot: {state, sessionID, modelName, totalTokens} after the last step}
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v2.0 (verified live 2026-08-27). Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/acp.rs acp_adapter_cases runs AcpAdapter, and rust/powerup-core/tests/acp_mock_agent.rs drives it against the mock itself and checks the "mock agent:" cases' lines and events against the mock's record. Swift: ACPFixtureTests.testAcpAdapterTable runs the whole table through CoreBridge.ACPStateMachine, the state machine ACPAdapter drives, and ACPAdapterIntegrationTests checks the "mock agent:" cases' lines against the real adapter and the mock, through the mock's record.
capturedAgainst: ACPAdapter.swift at dddf9c6 through a one-off differential harness, not kept in the tree (Swift 5.9.2, macOS 27.2), that checked every written line, every event, the state each event sees and the state after each step; the mock agent lines from acp-mock-agent.py run with /usr/bin/python3

cases.name: mock agent: the handshake gives sessionReady
cases.reason: HK-132: initialize declares protocol version 1 and no fs capability; session/new goes out only from the initialize response, with the project folder as cwd and an empty mcpServers; its result makes the session ready with the agent's current model. The lines are acp-mock-agent.py's; ACPAdapterIntegrationTests.testStartupHandshakeEmitsSessionReady checks them against the mock's record.

cases.name: mock agent: set_model accepted, then rejected
cases.reason: HK-148: an accepted switch changes the model and echoes the value asked for; a rejected one keeps the model and reports the agent's message. The lines are acp-mock-agent.py's; ACPAdapterIntegrationTests.testSetModelSuccessAndRejection checks them against the mock's record.

cases.name: a start without a command says so

event.message: No ACP agent command is configured — check Settings → General → Harness.

cases.reason: A harness with no agent command configured says where to fix it instead of spawning nothing; the state never leaves stopped, so nothing is published.

cases.name: a start with an empty command says so

event.message: No ACP agent command is configured — check Settings → General → Harness.

cases.reason: An empty command line is no command at all.

cases.name: an empty executable is spawned and fails there

event.message: Couldn't start the ACP agent (): The file doesn't exist.

cases.reason: Only a missing or empty command list is caught before the spawn; an empty executable fails in the spawn like any bad path.

cases.name: a failed spawn names the executable and the reason

event.message: Couldn't start the ACP agent (/missing/agent): The file “agent” doesn’t exist.

cases.reason: Process.run() throwing ends the launch with the path and the reason; nothing is written.

cases.name: an initialize error stops the agent

event.message: The ACP agent rejected initialize: unsupported protocol version

cases.reason: HK-147: a rejected initialize leaves no half-open session: the reason is reported, stdin closes, the state reads stopped, and the agent is killed after the grace.

cases.name: an initialize error without a message

event.message: The ACP agent rejected initialize:

cases.reason: HK-147: the error object alone is enough to stop; the message is empty.

cases.name: a session/new error without a message hints at logging in

event.message: The ACP agent couldn't create a session. Is it logged in? (e.g. run `opencode auth login`)

cases.reason: HK-147: an agent that is not logged in usually fails session/new without words, so the error suggests logging in (docs/harnesses.md quotes it).

cases.name: a session/new error reports its message

event.message: The ACP agent couldn't create a session: Authentication required

cases.reason: HK-147: the agent's own words explain the failure best.

cases.name: a session/new result without a sessionId fails

event.message: The ACP agent couldn't create a session. Is it logged in? (e.g. run `opencode auth login`)

cases.reason: HK-147: no session id means no session, even without an error.

cases.name: a session/new result that is not an object fails

event.message: The ACP agent couldn't create a session. Is it logged in? (e.g. run `opencode auth login`)

cases.reason: HK-403: result reads only as an object.

cases.name: a non-string sessionId fails

event.message: The ACP agent couldn't create a session. Is it logged in? (e.g. run `opencode auth login`)

cases.reason: HK-403: the session id reads only as a string.

cases.name: a session/new error with a sessionId still fails

event.message: The ACP agent couldn't create a session: quota

cases.reason: HK-147: an error wins over a result in the same response.

cases.name: an empty sessionId is accepted
cases.reason: Only a missing or non-string id fails; an empty string is a session id like any other.

cases.name: a session without models reports the model acp
cases.reason: opencode reports no models; sessionReady still needs a model name, so it says acp while the published model stays empty.

cases.name: a non-string currentModelId reads as no model
cases.reason: HK-403: the model reads only as a string; anything else is no model.

cases.name: a string error on initialize reads as success
cases.reason: HK-403: error reads only as an object, as Swift's cast did, so a string error does not stop the handshake.

cases.name: a send while starting is queued until the session is ready
cases.reason: HK-138: a prompt sent while the agent starts reads working at once and goes out after session/new; sessionReady keeps the working state.

cases.name: queued prompts go out one at a time
cases.reason: HK-138: prompts queued while starting go out first in, first out, the next only after the previous one's result.

cases.name: a send while working is queued until the result
cases.reason: HK-138: one prompt in flight at a time; the next goes out from the previous one's result.

cases.name: a send while stopped is refused

event.message: Can't send that — the agent session isn't running.

cases.reason: A prompt is never dropped silently: with no session it is refused with a message.

cases.name: a whitespace send does nothing
cases.reason: A prompt that trims to nothing is not sent and changes no state.

cases.name: a send is trimmed
cases.reason: Prompts are trimmed of whitespace and newlines, as Swift's trimmingCharacters did.

cases.name: a prompt keeps its newlines on one line
cases.reason: HK-153: a newline inside a prompt is escaped, so the message stays one line.

cases.name: the prompt result emits the reply, then the turn, then ready
cases.reason: HK-139, HK-405: the deltas stream as they come; the result emits the whole trimmed reply once, then turnCompleted while the adapter still reads working, and only then ready.

cases.name: a whitespace-only reply is no reply
cases.reason: HK-139: a reply that trims to nothing gives no reply event and no result text.

cases.name: a chunk outside a turn is cleared by the next prompt
cases.reason: HK-139: the reply buffer is cleared when a prompt goes out, so text streamed before it never joins its reply.

cases.name: a refusal is an error turn
cases.reason: HK-140: stopReason refusal counts as an error turn.

cases.name: a cancelled turn is not an error
cases.reason: HK-140: only refusal and a JSON-RPC error are errors; cancelled is an ordinary end.

cases.name: a prompt error reports its message
cases.reason: HK-140: a JSON-RPC error ends the turn as an error, with the agent's message as the detail.

cases.name: a prompt error without a message says error
cases.reason: HK-140: with no message the detail is error.

cases.name: a missing stopReason is end_turn
cases.reason: HK-140: a result without stopReason ended normally.

cases.name: a non-string stopReason is end_turn
cases.reason: HK-403: stopReason reads only as a string.

cases.name: an error beside a stopReason is still an error
cases.reason: HK-140: the error decides the turn and its detail even when the result names a stop reason.

cases.name: a string prompt error reads as success
cases.reason: HK-403: error reads only as an object, so a string error ends the turn normally.

cases.name: usage adds up across turns
cases.reason: HK-141: each prompt result adds its input and output tokens to the session total.

cases.name: zero usage leaves the total
cases.reason: HK-141: a turn's usage is added only when it is positive.

cases.name: usage counts the sum, not each side
cases.reason: HK-141: the sum decides, so a negative side lowers what is added.

cases.name: a fractional token count is truncated
cases.reason: HK-403: tokens read as NSNumber's intValue, which truncates toward zero.

cases.name: a bool token count reads as one
cases.reason: HK-403: true reads as 1 through NSNumber.

cases.name: a string token count reads as zero
cases.reason: HK-403: a string is not an NSNumber, so it counts as 0.

cases.name: usage that is not an object is ignored
cases.reason: HK-403: usage reads only as an object.

cases.name: set_model without a session is ignored
cases.reason: HK-148: with no session id nothing is sent, and nothing is queued for later either.

cases.name: set_model is trimmed and an empty one sends nothing
cases.reason: HK-148: the model is trimmed; an empty one sends nothing and takes no id.

cases.name: a set_model rejection without a message
cases.reason: HK-148: a rejection without words still explains itself; the model stays.

cases.name: a string set_model error reads as success
cases.reason: HK-403: error reads only as an object, so a string error switches the model.

cases.name: set_mode accepted and rejected
cases.reason: HK-148: the mode answer echoes the mode asked for; a rejection reports the agent's words, or a fallback; the published state never changes.

cases.name: a response nobody asked for is ignored
cases.reason: HK-146: a stray response (an id we never sent, or one already answered) changes nothing and never crashes.

cases.name: responses reach their requests in any order
cases.reason: HK-401: a response is matched by its id, not by the order the requests went out.

cases.name: an id of 1.0 matches request 1
cases.reason: HK-401: ids match through Swift's as? Int, which reads an integral number however it is written.

cases.name: an id of true matches request 1
cases.reason: HK-401: Swift's as? Int reads true as 1 (measured), so true answers request 1.

cases.name: a string or fractional id never matches
cases.reason: HK-401: "3" and 3.5 are not Ints, so they answer nothing; the real response still does.

cases.name: an agent request reusing a pending id is read as its response
cases.reason: HK-402: a message whose integer id is pending is that request's response even when it carries a method, as in Swift; the agent's request is swallowed.

cases.name: request ids keep counting across launches
cases.reason: HK-401: ids count from 1 per adapter and a new launch does not reset them, as Swift's nextRequestID was never reset.

cases.name: a response to a request of the old launch is dropped
cases.reason: HK-146: a start forgets every pending request, so the new agent's id 3 answers nothing it did not ask.

cases.name: mock agent: a prompt streams a reply, a tool and a permission, and completes
cases.reason: HK-131, HK-139, HK-141, HK-144, HK-151: a turn streams the reply but never the thought, shows the tool call, asks permission under the stringified rpc id, answers allow with the once option, then emits the whole reply and the usage; a second turn adds to the token total. The lines are acp-mock-agent.py's; ACPAdapterIntegrationTests.testPromptStreamsToolsPermissionAndCompletion checks them against the mock's record.

cases.name: answering allow picks the once option
cases.reason: HK-131, HK-144: the request becomes an event under its rpc id as text, and approving answers with the allow_once option, never allow_always.

cases.name: answering reject picks the reject_once option
cases.reason: HK-131: denying answers with reject_once, never reject_always.

cases.name: a permission is answered once
cases.reason: HK-144: answering removes the request, so a second answer and an id nobody asked about write nothing.

cases.name: no matching option answers cancelled
cases.reason: HK-131: with no option of the chosen direction the request is answered cancelled, never with the other direction.

cases.name: options with a non-object element answer cancelled
cases.reason: HK-403: options casts all-or-nothing to an array of objects, so one bad element leaves no option at all.

cases.name: an option without an optionId is skipped
cases.reason: HK-131: an option needs a string optionId; a missing kind reads as empty, which matches nothing.

cases.name: a repeated rpc id replaces the options
cases.reason: HK-407: a second request with the same id replaces the first one's options in place; it is answered once.

cases.name: a negative rpc id is an event id too
cases.reason: HK-144: any Int id works; the event id is its text.

cases.name: a permission asked while starting is answerable
cases.reason: HK-144: a permission request is served in any running state, before the session exists too.

cases.name: interrupt cancels each pending permission, then sends session/cancel
cases.reason: HK-143, HK-407: every unanswered permission is answered cancelled first, in arrival order, so the agent never hangs; then session/cancel goes out and the interrupt is reported done at once. The state stays working until the prompt's result.

cases.name: interrupt without a session does nothing
cases.reason: HK-143: with no session there is nothing to cancel; nothing is written or reported.

cases.name: interrupt when idle still reports done
cases.reason: HK-143: an interrupt with a session but no turn sends session/cancel and reports done; the agent ignores it.

cases.name: stop cancels pending permissions before stdin closes
cases.reason: HK-143, HK-154: unanswered permissions are answered cancelled while stdin is still open, then stdin closes, the state reads stopped with no session, and the kill is armed after the 2 s grace. The model stays.

cases.name: stop without a process does nothing

event.message: Couldn't start the ACP agent (/missing/agent): gone

cases.reason: HK-154: with nothing running a stop changes nothing.

cases.name: a second stop only arms another kill
cases.reason: HK-154: stdin is already closed, so a second stop before the exit only arms another kill after the grace.

cases.name: lines after a stop are dropped
cases.reason: HK-135: after a stop the pipe stays readable for the grace, but every line is dropped, so a dying agent's late permission request or reply cannot bring back a prompt the user just stopped; its exit is expected and silent.

cases.name: lines of a retired launch are dropped
cases.reason: HK-135: once a new launch starts, output, permission requests and the exit of the old one never touch it. A start while the old process has not exited stops it again, which arms another kill.

cases.name: a start while the agent runs stops it first
cases.reason: HK-135, HK-143: starting again stops the running agent first (its pending permission answered cancelled, stdin closed, the kill armed), then the new launch begins with a new generation; the old one's exit is ignored.

cases.name: an unexpected exit reports the stderr tail, then ended

event.message: Error: boom

cases.reason: HK-136: an exit nobody asked for shows the agent's last words, then ends the session.

cases.name: an unexpected exit with no stderr only ends
cases.reason: HK-136: with nothing on stderr there is no error event.

cases.name: an exit 0 nobody asked for still ends

event.message: done

cases.reason: HK-136: what makes an exit expected is the stop, not the code.

cases.name: an expected exit after a stop is silent
cases.reason: HK-136: after a stop the exit says nothing, whatever its code or stderr.

cases.name: an exit drops pending permissions without writing
cases.reason: HK-143, HK-407: stdin is gone with the process, so pending permissions are forgotten without an answer; answering one later writes nothing.

cases.name: an exit after an initialize error is silent

event.message: The ACP agent rejected initialize: no

cases.reason: HK-136, HK-147: the initialize error already stopped the agent, so its exit is expected.

cases.name: an exit while starting reports the tail

terminated.stderrTail: env: node: No such file or directory

event.message: env: node: No such file or directory

cases.reason: HK-136: an agent that dies during the handshake (a missing node, a bad flag) explains itself; its watchdog then does nothing.

cases.name: the watchdog stops a launch still starting

event.message: The ACP agent didn't finish starting within 30 seconds.

cases.reason: HK-134: an agent that has not finished the handshake within 30 seconds is reported and stopped, so the app never stays starting forever; its exit is then expected.

cases.name: the watchdog does nothing once ready
cases.reason: HK-134: a launch that finished starting is never stopped by its watchdog.

cases.name: a prompt queued while starting keeps the watchdog from firing
cases.reason: HK-406: the watchdog fires only while the state reads starting, and a prompt sent during the handshake already reads working, so that launch is never stopped by it (kept from Swift).

cases.name: a retired launch's watchdog does nothing

event.message: The ACP agent didn't finish starting within 30 seconds.

cases.reason: HK-134: the watchdog checks its own generation, so an old launch's timer never stops a newer launch that is still starting; the newer one's own timer does.
